text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually causes no symptoms at all, which is why it is often called the "silent killer". Many people can live with high blood pressure for years without realizing it while it slowly damages the heart, brain, and kidneys.

Symptoms generally only happen if your blood pressure climbs to dangerously high levels (a hypertensive crisis, defined as a reading over 180/120 mm Hg) or during extreme spikes. In those instances, you might experience:

list.snippet: Blood spots in the eyes (subconjunctival hemorrhage)

text_blocks.snippet: If your blood pressure reading is higher than 180/120 mm Hg, wait one minute and test it again. If it remains that high and you have any of the following emergency warning signs, call 911 immediately:
You can learn more about reading your numbers through the American Heart Association or review general risk guidelines from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
